description: Writes (or replaces) one analysis_results row for a run and analysis_type.
signature: def write_analysis_result(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, analysis_type: str, payload: dict, *, parameters_version: str) -> None
docstring:
Write one analysis result blob.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run this result belongs to.
    analysis_type: One of 'opportunity_matrix', 'tag_summary', 'tag_clusters', 'tag_trends', 'competition_density', 'funnel_report', 'case_studies'.
    payload: A JSON-serializable dict; stored verbatim as payload_json.
    parameters_version: The parameter-set hash in effect when this result was produced.

Returns:
    None.

Raises:
    StorageError: If run_id does not exist, analysis_type is not one of the seven allowed values, or payload is not JSON-serializable.
preconditions: analysis_type in the fixed seven-value set from the schema
payload is JSON-serializable (no non-finite floats such as NaN/Infinity, since strict JSON has no representation for them; callers must convert to null/None first)
postconditions: read_analysis_result(conn, run_id, analysis_type) returns exactly payload (deep-equal) after a successful write
Writing the same (run_id, analysis_type) again replaces the prior row (primary key is (run_id, analysis_type))

edge_cases.input: payload contains a float('nan') anywhere in the structure
edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError -- NaN is not valid JSON; callers must pre-convert to None
StorageError before any write is attempted

edge_cases.input: Writing the same (run_id, analysis_type) twice with different payloads
edge_cases.expected_behavior: the second write fully replaces the first; read_analysis_result reflects only the latest

unit_tests.name: test_write_then_read_roundtrip
unit_tests.description: A nested dict payload round-trips through write/read unchanged.

unit_tests.name: test_rewrite_replaces_prior_value
unit_tests.description: A second write for the same key overwrites the first.
unit_tests.expected: read_analysis_result reflects only the second payload

unit_tests.name: test_nan_in_payload_raises
unit_tests.description: A payload containing float('nan') raises StorageError.
unit_tests.expected: StorageError for an actual float('nan') value
